discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold bosons in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, the first clean realization of a strongly correlated quantum phase in a dilute atomic gas. This work turned cold atoms into a programmable laboratory for many-body physics. Building on it, the nominees developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution, observed antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization, entanglement entropy growth, and synthetic gauge fields. Zoller's theory (lattice gauge theories, Rydberg simulators) and the experimental breakthroughs of Bloch and Greiner established analog quantum simulation as a new field. It addresses central open problems in condensed matter physics and is a foundation of present quantum technologies. This is a new paradigm for studying quantum matter, not a refinement of an old one.
